title: Backyard Seismic Quiet-Hour Baseline Shift
app: Raspberry Shake, Safecast, Blitzortung-compatible lightning sensors, AirGradient CO2 sensors, radon monitors, allsky cameras, and magnetometers streamed to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=seismo:reading
| eval hour=tonumber(strftime(_time,"%H"))
| where hour>=1 AND hour<5
| bin _time span=1w
| stats avg(noise_floor) as quiet_noise_floor by station _time
| streamstats window=4 current=f avg(quiet_noise_floor) as baseline_noise_floor by station
| where baseline_noise_floor>0 AND quiet_noise_floor>baseline_noise_floor*1.2
| sort - quiet_noise_floor
description: Uses Quiet-hour seismic noise telemetry to monitor changes in the normal overnight noise baseline in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for new vibration sources near the sensor before they hide real events, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Quiet-hour seismic noise data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a hourly cadence.
grandmaExplanation: It turns changes in the normal overnight noise baseline so you can spot new vibration sources near the sensor before they hide real events before it becomes annoying.
